key_terms.حَمٓ: Disjointed letters Ha and Mim, appearing at the start of Surah Ghafir.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the letters Ha Mim in the Quran?
ai.summary: In the chapter Al-Ghafir (The Forgiver), these disjointed letters (al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at) serve as a divine challenge to the skeptics of Mecca, emphasizing the Quran's miraculous and inimitable nature. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, often interpret these letters as an invitation to reflect on the divine origin of the text, linking them to the attributes of Allah as the All-Forgiving and All-Knowing. This opening sets the tone for the chapter's narrative of Pharaoh's denial and the ultimate triumph of faith.
